title: rhize-context-manager stack inventory configuration
description: Optional config read by the context-stack skill's routing logic at $HOME/.claude/rhize-context-manager/stack.config.json, and WRITTEN by /context-setup after the user confirms a proposed per-repo stack. When present, `layers` is the authoritative tool-stack inventory (which layers exist, where they run, which repos they cover) instead of the skill's built-in default inventory. schemaVersion 2 adds `repoOverrides`: per-repo enable/disable decisions with reasons, so /context-setup can record a decision for one repo (e.g. "disable claude-mem here, OpenWolf already covers it") without mutating the shared `layers` catalog that other repos also read. This file is the schema/documentation only; it contains no real values.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped from the unversioned v1 shape (layers only) when repoOverrides was added. No real file existed under v1, so there is no migration path to preserve — v2 is the only version any writer should produce.

layers.description: Ordered list of stack layers, most-relevant-first (the order the skill should consider them in when routing a question).

repoOverrides.description: Keyed by repo name (matches a `layers[].repos` entry / repo directory basename). Written by /context-setup. Read-side rule: for the current repo, start from `layers` (a layer applies if scope is "global", or scope is "per-repo" and the repo name is in `repos`), then apply this repo's `decisions` on top — `enabled: false` suppresses a layer for this repo even if `layers` would otherwise include it; `enabled: true` adds coverage without editing the shared `repos` list.

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the /context-setup run that produced these decisions.

reason.description: One-line justification shown to the user at proposal time, e.g. "redundant with CodeGraph, already indexed here".

layer.description: Which problem class this layer addresses: wire = API/CLI traffic compression, memory = persistent/cross-session recall, file-intel = in-session file indexing/corrections, index = symbol/code navigation, cli = terminal-output compression.

scope.description: global = runs the same way for every repo/session. per-repo = only active where explicitly installed/configured; see `repos`.

repos.description: Repo names this layer is active in. Required in practice when scope is 'per-repo' and coverage is a fixed list rather than 'every repo that opts in'.

endpoints.description: Named endpoints/ports this layer exposes, e.g. { "proxy": "127.0.0.1:8787", "dashboard": "http://localhost:37777" }.

notes.description: What problem this layer solves and any coexistence caveats (overlap risks with other layers, etc.).

layers.name: Example Wire Proxy
layers.notes: Compresses API traffic for the listed repos via a git-ignored local settings file.

layers.name: Example Global Memory
layers.notes: Persistent cross-session observation memory; injects recalled context at session start.

decisions.reason: Repo already runs a per-repo file-intel layer with correction hooks; the global memory layer duplicated its recall.
